prompt:
`node build.mjs` in this project is supposed to build a small site from the documents in `my docs/input files` into a folder named `build output`. It fails or produces wrong output because the folder names contain spaces and some file names contain spaces, apostrophes, ampersands, parentheses and other punctuation (for example `Dad's Notes.md`, `O'Brien & Sons orders.csv`, `notes (draft).txt`, `Zeta double space.md` with two spaces, `Q&A $& more.md`). Fix build.mjs (and the helper tools in tools/ if they need it) so that running `node build.mjs` from the project folder creates exactly the following files in `build output` and nothing else: - `pages/.html` for every .md file, rendered by tools/render-md.mjs. - `tables/.html` for every .csv file, rendered by tools/csv-table.mjs. - `raw/` for every other file (including files with no extension, files whose name starts with a dot, binary files and empty files), copied byte for byte with its original file name, keeping the folders it has under `my docs/input files`. For example `raw/images/team photo.svg` and `raw/notes (draft).txt`. - `index.html`: the template `my docs/templates/page template.html` with every `{{title}}` replaced by `Site index` and `{{links}}` replaced by one line `
  • Dad's Notes
    • ` for each page and each table (the href is relative to `build output`, written with forward slashes), sorted by the output path (compared as plain code units, the default JavaScript sort) and joined with \n. The link text is the input file name without its extension, with & < > " and ' escaped as & < > " '. The replacements are literal text, so a file name such as `Q&A $& more` must appear in the index exactly as its escaped link text. - `manifest.json`: a JSON array with 2 space indentation and a trailing newline, with one object per file under `my docs/input files`, with the keys in this order: `source`, `output`, `sha256`. `source` and `output` are paths relative to the project folder written with forward slashes on every platform, for example "my docs/input files/Dad's Notes.md" and "build output/pages/dads-notes.html". `sha256` is the lower case hex SHA-256 of the output file (tools/checksum.mjs prints it). The entries are sorted by `source`, comparing the strings as plain code units (the default JavaScript sort), so uppercase letters sort before lowercase letters and `!` and `-` sort before letters. The `` is made from the input file name without its extension: lower case it, remove apostrophes, turn every run of other characters that are not a-z or 0-9 into a single hyphen (so `Café Menu` becomes `caf-menu`), and remove hyphens from both ends. If nothing is left, the slug is `untitled`. So `Dad's Notes` becomes `dads-notes`, `O'Brien & Sons orders` becomes `obrien-sons-orders` and `Zeta double space` becomes `zeta-double-space`. File extensions are matched ignoring case (`SHOUT.MD` is a Markdown file). When two files that go to the same output folder (`pages` or `tables`) get the same slug, the one whose `source` sorts first in the manifest order keeps the slug, and the next ones get `-2`, `-3` and so on added to the slug (for example `dads-notes.html` and `dads-notes-2.html`). The tools must handle what the inputs contain. Input files may use LF or CRLF line endings, and the generated pages and tables must not contain a carriage return. A CSV file follows these rules: fields are separated by commas; a field that starts with a double quote is quoted, and inside it a comma, a line break (kept in the cell as a single \n) and a doubled quote (one quote character in the cell) are part of the text; a double quote anywhere else in a field is an ordinary character; empty lines are skipped; the last record may have no line ending. A second mode: `node build.mjs --check` builds nothing and changes nothing. It reads `build output/manifest.json` and prints one line per manifest entry, in manifest order, to standard output: `ok ` when the file exists and its SHA-256 equals the recorded `sha256`, `changed ` when it exists with a different SHA-256, or `missing ` when it does not exist (`` is the entry's `output` string, for example `ok build output/pages/dads-notes.html`). It prints nothing else to standard output and exits with 0 when every line is `ok` and 1 otherwise. When `build output/manifest.json` does not exist it prints `no manifest` to standard error, prints nothing to standard output and exits with 2. Files in `build output` that are not in the manifest are ignored. Also: a normal build must delete `build output` at the start so an old file never stays, running it twice in a row must work, and it must work when the project folder itself is in a path with spaces. Do not rename, move or edit the files under `my docs`.
